name: Belle and Sebastian
label: Matador
lede: A church-hall caretaker just out of seven years of illness, a college course for unemployed musicians, 1,000 copies of a debut, and a band that sent friends to pose for its photos.

eras.title: A course for the unemployed
eras.text: Stuart Murdoch spent seven years too ill to work, then found his songs through a Glasgow government-funded music course and a college record label that only meant to put out a single. Two albums arrived inside six months of 1996.

years.src: Wikipedia: Stuart Murdoch (musician) · Wikipedia: Stuart David · Wikipedia: If You're Feeling Sinister
years.h: Stuart Murdoch meets Stuart David on the Beatbox course
years.p: Murdoch, recovering from years of ME/chronic fatigue syndrome, meets bassist [[Stuart David|2854838c-9119-4d95-9a44-394d05481bf5]] on Beatbox, a Stow College programme for unemployed musicians in Glasgow.
years.xp:
Murdoch was diagnosed with ME/CFS in the late 1980s and couldn't work for seven years. By early 1995 he had largely recovered. He and David first played together in bands called Lisa Helps the Blind and Rhode Island.

Murdoch lived above and worked as caretaker for the church hall at Hyndland Parish Church until 2003. The band rehearsed in the hall.

years.h: Stow College's Electric Honey label offers an album, not a single
years.p: Impressed by the demos, the college's music business course, led by former Associates member Alan Rankine, lets Murdoch make a full album on its student-run label.

years.src: Wikipedia: Belle and Sebastian · Wikipedia: Isobel Campbell · Wikipedia: Tigermilk
years.h: Recruiting a band at the Grosvenor Café
years.p: Murdoch and David enlist [[Stevie Jackson|32afcb9a-787b-44ed-b5db-c6ea8ffb5ab1]], [[Isobel Campbell|d51f3a15-12a2-41a0-acfa-33b5eae71164]], [[Chris Geddes|6cd0aebf-b60e-46a3-8052-9976d9900127]] and David's flatmate [[Richard Colburn|e7528aba-c5e2-4917-9a52-9b61d56f9a13]]. The name comes from a Murdoch story based on the 1965 TV series about a boy and his Pyrenean mountain dog, Belle.
years.xp: Isobel Campbell was nineteen when she met Murdoch at a New Year's Eve party. Richard Colburn was a student on the Stow College music business course.

years.cap: Tigermilk, Electric Honey, 1996. Photo of Joanne Kenney by Stuart Murdoch
years.h: Tigermilk: 1,000 vinyl copies, recorded in three days
years.p: Cut mostly live at CaVa in Glasgow, March 4–6, 1996. Electric Honey presses 1,000 LPs. They sell out within months, and by 1999 an original was worth $600.
years.xp:
John Peel and Mark Radcliffe played it on BBC radio, which led to a session and a record deal. Murdoch took the cover photo of his then-girlfriend Joanne Kenney; the toy in the picture was auctioned for charity in 2019.

Jeepster reissued it properly in 1999, and it has since sold more than 124,000 copies.

years.h: Belle and Sebastian sign to Jeepster
years.p: The response to Tigermilk earns the band a deal with London's Jeepster Records. Violinist [[Sarah Martin|b97377be-453d-4a1b-b40e-72cff3cfefd4]] joins just before the next sessions.

years.h: If You're Feeling Sinister, made in five days
years.p: Recorded at CaVa with Tony Doogan and mixed in three days. Murdoch shot the cover of his friend Ciara MacLaverty, who also had chronic fatigue syndrome. Pitchfork gave it 10/10.
years.xp:
Sarah Martin compared making Tigermilk and Sinister back to back to the Beatles cutting Rubber Soul and Revolver. Spin later named it one of the 100 greatest albums of 1985–2005, and Pitchfork ranked it No. 14 of the 1990s.

Matador released it in the US in 1997.
play: The Stars of Track and Field

eras.title: The band that wouldn't pose
eras.text: Belle and Sebastian barely toured, rarely spoke to the press and sent friends to stand in for photos. Three EPs climbed the UK chart anyway, and Matador Records took them to America.

years.h: No interviews, no photos: friends pose instead
years.p: While Stuart Murdoch recovers his health, the band keeps a deliberately low profile, plays rarely and refuses publicity photos, often asking friends to pose in its place. The mystery becomes part of the appeal.

years.h: Dog on Wheels EP reaches No. 59
years.p: The first EP features Murdoch, Stuart David and trumpeter [[Mick Cooke|b6291b68-d71b-4dae-99c8-0e279dff82b5]], who won't officially join for another year.

years.h: Lazy Line Painter Jane, recorded in Murdoch's church
years.p: The EP is cut in the church where Stuart Murdoch lives, with [[Monica Queen|9a86679d-7661-4633-b1b0-76a69922458c]] singing. It reaches No. 41.

years.h: 3.. 6.. 9 Seconds of Light: the first top-40 hit
years.p: NME and Melody Maker both make it Single of the Week, and it reaches No. 32.

years.src: Wikipedia: The Boy with the Arab Strap
years.h: The Boy with the Arab Strap reaches UK No. 12
years.p: Released by Jeepster and, in America, by Matador. More members write and sing: Stevie Jackson leads two songs, Isobel Campbell one, Stuart David speaks one. Mick Cooke joins as a full member.
years.xp: It sold 200,000 copies through 2006. Pitchfork gave it 0.8 out of 10, calling it a parody of the earlier albums, then pulled that review and re-scored it 8.5 in 2018.
play: The Boy with the Arab Strap
The Boy with the Arab Strap

q: There's a limit to putting someone else's name on an album.
years.src: Wikipedia: The Boy with the Arab Strap
years.h: The title annoys Arab Strap, the band
years.p: Stuart Murdoch borrowed the name of the Falkirk duo [[Arab Strap|6caf09f5-2f01-4f76-bcc7-6207930c56c6]], who had toured with them, and didn't know it was also a sex aid. Arab Strap were not pleased.

eras.title: A Brit Award, and the band splits in two
eras.text: A surprise win over Steps made them tabloid news and a hit singles band. Then the founding bassist left to write novels, the cellist walked out mid-tour, and they left Jeepster.

years.h: Beating Steps for Best British Breakthrough at the Brits
years.p: At the London Arena, Belle and Sebastian, three albums in, win the Radio 1 listener vote. Next day the press alleges students at two universities rigged the online poll.
years.xp: Steps were among the biggest pop acts in Britain. Defenders pointed out that the band naturally appealed to students, that Isobel Campbell had attended one of the universities named, and that awards ought to reflect artistic merit rather than sales.

years.h: The first Bowlie Weekender
years.p: Belle and Sebastian host their own festival. Twenty years later they revive it on a Mediterranean cruise ship.

years.h: Fold Your Hands Child, You Walk Like a Peasant
years.p: The band's first UK top-ten album, though critics felt it was stagnating. Legal Man, co-written by Isobel Campbell, reaches No. 15 and gets them on Top of the Pops.

years.h: Jack Black mocks them in High Fidelity
years.p: In the film, Jack Black's record-store clerk dismisses Belle and Sebastian as old sad bastard music. A clip of Seymour Stein plays in the scene.

years.h: Stuart David leaves for Looper and his novels
years.p: The co-founder quits to concentrate on Looper and books; his first novel, Nalda Said, came out in 1999. [[Bobby Kildea|02807e7c-66a4-4d8c-8abc-7b94d089bd85]] of V-Twin replaces him.

years.h: Storytelling soundtrack for Todd Solondz
years.p: Belle and Sebastian spend much of the year touring and scoring the Todd Solondz film.

years.src: Wikipedia: Isobel Campbell · Wikipedia: Belle and Sebastian
years.h: Isobel Campbell walks out in the middle of a North American tour
years.p: Campbell leaves Belle and Sebastian partway through the US and Canadian dates to go solo. She later makes three albums with [[Mark Lanegan|a9126556-f555-4920-9617-6e013f8228a7]], including the Mercury-nominated Ballad of the Broken Seas.
years.xp: She had already made records as The Gentle Waves in 1999 and 2000. The BBC Sessions album (2008) includes some of her last recordings with the band.

years.h: Leaving Jeepster for Rough Trade
years.p: Belle and Sebastian sign a four-album deal with Rough Trade Records. Matador keeps releasing them in America.

eras.title: Trevor Horn and the Hollywood Bowl
eras.text: A pop producer, a Thin Lizzy tribute and their biggest hits turned the shy band into a big one, capped by 18,000 people and an orchestra in Los Angeles.

years.h: Dear Catastrophe Waitress, produced by Trevor Horn
years.p: Stuart Murdoch returns as main songwriter, and the band aims for the radio with the man behind [[The Buggles|20278bbd-271a-4a1c-b6fd-43a13d43203d]] and [[Frankie Goes to Hollywood|c09c8263-40ef-4352-8031-e438b1ce68fc]]. It restores their indie credibility.

years.h: I'm a Cuckoo, their Thin Lizzy song, reaches No. 14
years.p: The single is their highest UK chart placing yet, and the band earns Mercury Prize and Ivor Novello nominations.

years.h: A War on Want trip to Israel and the Palestinian territories
years.p: Members visit with the UK charity. It leads to the song The Eighth Station of the Cross Kebab House, later a B-side of Funny Little Frog.

years.h: The Life Pursuit: UK No. 8 and a US chart debut
years.p: Produced by Tony Hoffer and recorded in California, first planned as a double album. It reaches No. 65 on the Billboard 200. Funny Little Frog debuts at No. 13 in the UK.

q: This is the biggest thrill of my entire life.
years.h: The Hollywood Bowl, with the LA Philharmonic
years.p: Belle and Sebastian play a sold-out Hollywood Bowl, 18,000 people, with the Los Angeles Philharmonic. [[The Shins|6c8b9855-ba8b-48f9-ac1d-42167f7f7b18]] open.

eras.title: Bowlie, cruise ships and a drummer left in North Dakota
eras.text: After four years away from British stages the band settled into a long, steady middle age: festivals, a film, a trumpeter's exit and the funniest tour story in their history.

years.h: First UK gig in almost four years, at Latitude
years.p: About 30,000 people see the band at Henham Park in Suffolk, where they preview new songs.

years.h: Write About Love, with Norah Jones and Carey Mulligan
years.p: The eighth album reaches UK No. 8. [[Norah Jones|985c709c-7771-4de3-9024-7bda29ebe3f9]] sings on one song and actor Carey Mulligan on the title track.

years.h: Mick Cooke leaves on good terms
years.p: The trumpeter, in the band since 1998, confirms his exit.

years.h: Stuart Murdoch's God Help the Girl premieres at Sundance
years.p: Murdoch wrote and directed the musical film in 2012–13.

years.h: Girls in Peacetime Want to Dance, recorded in Atlanta
years.p: Belle and Sebastian's ninth album is the first with touring bassist Dave McGowan of [[Teenage Fanclub|e6f8912b-7df9-4aae-b551-2cd03dc29588]]. In June they play Glastonbury's Other Stage.

years.h: The band leaves Richard Colburn at a North Dakota Walmart
years.p: On a US tour, Belle and Sebastian accidentally drive off without their drummer.

years.h: Dave McGowan becomes an official member
years.p: The Teenage Fanclub bassist, touring with the band since 2011, joins for good. Three How to Solve Our Human Problems EPs came out from December 2017 to February 2018.

years.h: The Boaty Weekender, on a cruise ship
years.p: For the 20th anniversary of the first Bowlie, the band throws its festival on a Mediterranean cruise. The Days of the Bagnold Summer soundtrack follows.

eras.title: Two albums in eight months
eras.text: Nearly thirty years in, Belle and Sebastian released a new album, then surprised everyone with another.

years.h: A Bit of Previous
years.p: Belle and Sebastian's eleventh studio album.

years.h: Late Developers, a surprise album
years.p: Announced without warning, with I Don't Know What You See in Me out on January 9 and the album four days later.
play: I Don't Know What You See in Me
